outlook: Grains were mixed at midday Monday: December corn was up about a penny at $4.46 3/4 and Minneapolis December spring wheat was a few cents higher near $6.30, while January soybeans slipped about 5 cents to $12.26 and Chicago wheat was lower. Outside markets are weighing on prices, with crude oil and stocks falling sharply and the U.S. dollar index reaching a 19-month high. Corn is getting support from last week's marketing-year-high export sales, and soybean sales to China continued after a virtual U.S.–China trade meeting, with Trump and Xi scheduled to meet at APEC this week. Traders are also watching a holiday-delayed CFTC fund-position report and this afternoon's Crop Progress report.
